lies.feedback: You found the contradiction and put it to her, but as an accusation. She held to her story and you never learned what was behind it.
lies.patient_claim: I take my metformin every day.
lies.truth: She skips most doses because of GI side effects and cost.
lies.reveal_condition: Asked non-judgmentally about side effects or cost, or shown the refill history.

under_probing.why_it_mattered: The side effects and the cost are the cause of the missed doses. A plan that ignores them asks her to do what she already cannot.

behaviors.feedback: After she said "I said I take it," you moved on to the next task and left the tension where it was.

strengths: Checked the pharmacy record instead of accepting her answer.
Linked the high HbA1c to missed doses and did not propose raising the dose.
improvements: When the chart contradicts the patient, share what you see and ask what gets in the way. Do not ask why she said otherwise.
Acknowledge loss and fear when the patient brings them up.
Use open, concrete questions about diet.
next_attempt_suggestions: Try: "The pharmacy shows two fills since spring. A lot of people have trouble with this one. What's it been like for you?"
When her arms cross, stop and name it: "I think I came at that the wrong way."
